chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Raḥīm, who said:

I said to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: I see that when you pray, and you raise your head from sajdah in the first and third rakʿah, you sit upright and then stand. So should we do as you do? He said: Do not look at what I do; do what you are commanded.

He عليه السلام only said, 'Do not look at what I do,' so that they would not believe that this was obligatory upon them by way of obligation, not that he had forbidden them from following his act as a matter of merit and perfection. This sitting is among the etiquettes of salat (prayer), not among its obligatory acts, and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.آدَابِ الصَّلَاةِ: the etiquettes and recommended manners of salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا تَنْظُرُوا إِلَى مَا أَصْنَعُ: do not treat my personal action as itself establishing obligation for you
key_terms.مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ: what you have been commanded to do as your binding duty

ai.seo_question: Is sitting briefly after sajdah before standing in salat (prayer) obligatory or recommended?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Imam’s brief sitting after the second sajdah before standing was not meant to be understood as an obligatory part of salat (prayer). Rather, it is presented as one of the etiquettes and recommended perfections of prayer, while the binding duty remains what one has been commanded.
